digest.claim_restated: On Hegel's Objectivity ladder (mechanism → chemism → teleology), the partition/Φ criterion reaches only the top of mechanism and reports the same aggregate/configuration cut Hegel draws at the base — but the two orderings run on different axes (Hegel grades self-determination, the instrument grades resistance to partition), so they cross inside the chemical process and part decisively at teleology, where Hegel replaces the criterion with inner purposiveness rather than anticipating a causal one; the homology is same-boundary/different-instrument, never "Hegel anticipated Φ."
digest.post:
GROUNDING DIGEST — Post 4, "Where Hegel Files the Microscope" (draft v3)

State of the draft. v3 already absorbed the five-reviewer v2 panel (posts/post4_reviews/). Every major v2 finding is closed in the current text: the crossing is decomputed and restaged inside the chemical process (pp. 647–649), the false "ranks below the solar system" leg is gone, "chemism is that case, run" is now "read, not run," Ebeturk is recast as dissent rather than support, the "higher principle" quote is re-attributed to teleology-in-general, the Life-chapter quotes are placed one division above Objectivity past §213, the plough splice and Kant pronoun/index are fixed, the "anticipation" tripwire is now "description," the apparatus logic-flip and Φ citation are fixed, and "each shorter than the last" is corrected to "chemism is the shortest." Fresh grounding confirms these fixes hold and surfaces no new refuting scholarship.

Primary text. The di Giovanni Science of Logic quotations are verifiable verbatim against the archive.org print scan (the Hegel-specialist reviewer read pp. 640–650, 653–654, 660, 663–664, 680–681 directly); this grounding pass re-confirmed the article and edition metadata but did not re-open the scan line by line, so those loci carry "verified" on the specialist's direct check. The two B&D Encyclopedia pins (§194 Addition 2 at p. 270; §204 Remark at p. 277) remain one-source and gated — physical spot-check owed. Kant Guyer/Matthews quotations (Ak 5:370–376, 5:400) are verified against published reproductions.

Secondary. Kreines 2008 (anchor + threat) grounds the "Hegel wins the classification" move and supplies the replacement, not anticipation, reading; page pins (pp. 344–377; p. 346 quotes) rest on the Wayback CUP galley and need a printed-volume check. Ng 2020 (the sharpest threat, load-bearing for the no-anticipation guard) — chapter 2 title confirmed via OUP/NDPR; the draft quotes nothing of her and says so, so her page pins stay open but non-blocking. Ebeturk 2023 (Hegel Bulletin 44/1, pp. 46–73) confirmed via Cambridge Core, including that his thesis runs opposite to a concession (teleology "misplaced," Life should follow chemism directly) — the draft now takes his p. 57 sentence for the axis it names, not the verdict. Koch 2023 (same issue, pp. 148–170) confirmed; used as the object-constitution prior-art the instrument cannot parse.

New context. Ebeturk and Koch both sit in the "Hegel and Teleology" special issue of Hegel Bulletin 44/1 (2023) — a contextual detail the draft could note but need not. No scholarship newer than 2026-07-10 changes the picture. Two unverified leads surfaced and are flagged below.

Lab bridge. The bridge is homology at its correct altitude: the instrument brackets self-maintenance, and the corpus has "receipts for recovery, none for reproduction." That claim is accurate to the code — probe_resilience.py (Probe 108) measures recovery time after a node flip; probe_attractor_condition.py (Probe 130) tests fixed-point collapse as a verdict predictor; STRUCTURAL_FINDINGS #7 records that cheap proxies recover the verdict only near chance (rank-AUC ≤ 0.63) and that exact Φ is needed and feasible only because coordination units are small (verdicts live at n=3–6). Nothing in the corpus models a chemical pair or self-production; the draft states this plainly. The owed computation (acid–medium–base toy) stays owed, and the draft says the crossing is a reading until it runs.

Guard. Clean on both prohibited moves: the draft explicitly refuses the anticipation reading ("He does not anticipate a causal-irreducibility criterion... He replaces it") and never calls Φ decorative, hollow, unnecessary, or a calculator ("The instrument's contribution is not diminished by having a ceiling"). One watch-item, not a breach: the author-owned temper paragraph in "What the Bracketing Buys" aims its "cannot be wrong because it cannot be run" barb at Hegel's criterion (legitimate), but the surrounding "I mind conceding the classification more than the papers before this one" flirts with the self-defeating register CLAUDE.md warns against. It does not demote Φ; the author must own or soften it.

primary_passages.quote_or_paraphrase: Objectivity "contains the three forms: mechanism, chemism, and the relation of purpose" — the ladder statement.
"The object" division opens at §194 and runs to §213, where "the idea" begins — fixes where Objectivity ends and the Life chapter (Idea) begins.
"The chemical object is distinguished from the mechanical in that... in the chemical object the determinateness, and hence the reference to other... belong to its nature."
"A chemical object is not comprehensible from itself, and the being of one object is the being of another"; the extremes "tensed against each other."

"their opposition and tension are thereby blunted... the striving attains its tranquil neutrality"; "only a formal unity"; "the capacity for their prior self-subsistence and tension is retained"; "The process does not spontaneously re-start itself, for it had non-indifference only as its presupposition – it did not posit it"; water/sign/language as the medium of the tensed extremes.

"these three syllogisms fall apart"; the process is "extinguished in this product and is re-activated only by a differentiation that comes to it from outside" — Hegel's own bookkeeping, the syllogisms falling apart where free mechanism's closed.

Kant's "greatest services" (external vs internal purposiveness, opening the concept of life); "the higher principle, the concept in its concrete existence... a principle of freedom." CORRECTED in v3: attached to teleology-in-general, before the external/internal distinction, not to inner purposiveness.
"Through the concept of inner purposiveness, Kant re-awakened the idea in general and that of life in particular."

External purposiveness's content "externally given... in the manifoldness of the objective world" (653); a means "is only a merely mechanical object" (660); the plough/cunning-of-reason passage — "the plough is more honorable than are immediately the enjoyments" (663; CORRECTED: the MEANS outranks the purpose); "in the teleological transition, what maintains itself is the concept that as such already concretely exists as cause" (664).

primary_passages.locus: SL pp. 680–681 (Life chapter, Section III The Idea)
primary_passages.quote_or_paraphrase: Living thing taken as "a whole consisting of parts... the individual itself" left "as something dead" (680); externality "a manifold, not of parts but of members" (681); each member driven "to produce itself" and "to sublate itself and make itself a means for the other" (681). PLACEMENT CORRECTED in v3: one division above Objectivity, past §213 — strengthens the Paper 5 handoff.

primary_passages.edition: Guyer & Matthews (Cambridge 2000), Critique of the Power of Judgment
primary_passages.quote_or_paraphrase: Natural end "cause and effect of itself" (5:370–71); parts "reciprocally the cause and effect of their form" (5:373–74); "not a mere machine... formative power" and nature "organizes itself" (5:374; pronoun CORRECTED to nature); natural end "not a constitutive concept... but... a regulative concept" (5:375–76); no "Newton... of a blade of grass," "absurd for humans" (5:400; index to human insight kept).

secondary_sources.work: Kreines, "The Logic of Life: Hegel's Philosophical Defense of Teleological Explanation of Living Beings," in Beiser (ed.), Cambridge Companion to Hegel and 19th-Century Philosophy (2008), ch. 13, pp. 344–377
secondary_sources.key_claim: Living beings "do manifest true 'internal purposiveness,'" "explicable in teleological terms," and "we can have objective knowledge of this natural teleology" (p. 346); "Hegel accords great philosophical importance to Kant's discussions of teleology... and yet also disagrees with Kant's central conclusions" (p. 344). Grounds "Hegel wins the classification" as replacement, not anticipation.

secondary_sources.work: Ng, Hegel's Concept of Life: Self-Consciousness, Freedom, Logic (OUP 2020)
secondary_sources.key_claim: Inner purposiveness moves regulative→constitutive and becomes the shape of the Concept as such; life "opens up the space of reasons." Load-bearing for the no-anticipation guard: if the organism stands where it stands because it is self-producing, reading teleology as partition-irreducibility imports the synchronic mechanism Hegel rejects. Ch. 2 title "'Kant's Great Service to Philosophy'" confirmed. Draft quotes nothing of hers and says so.

secondary_sources.work: Ebeturk, "Between Chemism and Life: Is Hegel's Teleology Misplaced?" Hegel Bulletin 44/1 (2023), pp. 46–73
secondary_sources.key_claim: Argues teleology is misplaced and "the logic of 'Life' and internal teleology should precede" external teleology, allowing "a direct passage from 'Chemism' to 'Life'" (p. 46). His p. 57 sentence ("the chemical process as a whole is the self-determination of the concept in and through distinctive objective processes") powers a counter-verdict, not a concession — v3 now takes it for the axis it names.

secondary_sources.work: Koch, "Mechanism, External Purposiveness, and Object Individuation: from Mechanism to Teleology in Hegel's Science of Logic," Hegel Bulletin 44/1 (2023), pp. 148–170
secondary_sources.key_claim: "Structures of external purposiveness constitute mechanical objects" (p. 149); "there are no objects without such teleological structures. The constitution of objects is ontologically dependent on teleological structures" (p. 162). The instrument's given "parts" are downstream of a purposive individuation the causal register cannot represent.

new_scholarship.relevance: Ebeturk and Koch both sit in the 'Hegel and Teleology' special issue of Hegel Bulletin 44/1 (2023). Not newer than the cutoff, but a contextual detail the draft could note to frame the intra-Hegelian ordering dispute as a live scholarly field rather than two isolated articles.

PhilPapers surfaced a Ng item 'The Objectivity of the Concept' (rec NGTOOW) treating the Mechanism/Chemism/Teleology chapters directly — possibly a separate chapter/essay distinct from the 2020 book. Worth a check as a sharper statement of the threat, but not verified in this pass.
A workshop 'Teleology in Hegel's Logic' (PhilEvents event 83158) indicates active current work; the page 403'd, so date/participants/output are unconfirmed. Flag only — do not cite.

This is the 'recovery' half of the draft's 'receipts for recovery, none for reproduction.'

lab_receipts.receipt: STRUCTURAL_FINDINGS #7: cheap ΦID / whole-minus-sum proxies separate dyadic from triadic only near chance; exact Φ is needed and feasible only because coordination units are small — backs the draft's 'answerable in principle, answered in practice at the sizes coordination units actually come in.'

The draft's decompute flag ('nothing in this section is computed... the corpus contains no chemical pair') and its owed acid–medium–base toy are accurate to the corpus.

digest.refutation_condition: Built for Hegel to win the classification and the lab to win the method. The honest form, per Ng and Kreines: Hegel replaces the unity criterion with inner teleology; he does not anticipate a causal one. The post fails if it smuggles proto-Φ back in through the win — if it lets partition-irreducibility become what Hegel's teleology "was really measuring," a reviewer holding Ng will say the reading imports the exact synchronic, cut-from-outside mechanism Hegel's ladder is built to escape. It also fails if either side sweeps: if the lab demotes Hegel's classification to a mere calculator-verdict, or if the concession tips into demoting Φ. The crossing inside chemism (pp. 647–649) is the load-bearing exhibit that makes the anticipation reading false rather than merely disavowed; if that crossing were removed or shown to depend on an uncomputed cross-system comparison, the paper's one original result collapses to "our formalism is decidable and Hegel's criterion is not," which is table stakes, not a finding.
digest.guard_check: Clean on both prohibited moves. (1) Anticipation: the draft explicitly refuses it — "He does not anticipate a causal-irreducibility criterion and wait for someone to compute it. He replaces it" — and the v2 tripwire phrase "cleaner anticipation" is now "cleaner description" (line 160). The word "anticipation" survives only in the guard/negative sense. (2) Demotion of Φ: no sentence calls Φ decorative, hollow, unnecessary, or a calculator; the draft affirms "The instrument's contribution is not diminished by having a ceiling" and "A tool that could not say where its ceiling is would be the one to distrust." ONE WATCH-ITEM, not a breach: the author-owned temper paragraph in "What the Bracketing Buys" ("There are days I think 'richer' is what we call a criterion that cannot be wrong because it cannot be run... I mind conceding the classification more than the papers before this one minded theirs") aims its barb correctly at Hegel's criterion, but the surrounding register drifts toward the self-defeating tone CLAUDE.md flags (modest ≠ self-defeating). It does not demote Φ; the author must own or soften it before posting — the sourcing note already marks this as the one paragraph the author must ratify.
digest.gates: Physical/paywalled checks still owed before citation is final: (1) B&D Encyclopedia pagination is one-source — spot-check §194 Addition 2 at p. 270 and §204 Remark at p. 277 against a print Brinkmann–Dahlstrom volume. (2) Kreines "Logic of Life" page pins (pp. 344–377; p. 346 quotes) rest on the Wayback-captured June 2008 CUP galley — a library check against the printed Cambridge Companion volume closes it; also confirm the italicized "Critique of Reason" typesetting inside the di Giovanni p. 654 block quote at proof. (3) Ng page pins remain open (draft quotes nothing of hers, so non-blocking) — verify only if any Ng wording is later quoted. (4) Verify the Ng "The Objectivity of the Concept" lead (PhilPapers NGTOOW) is not a sharper separate statement of the threat worth citing. (5) Non-source gate: the owed acid–medium–base toy computation (mid-reaction vs neutralized rule-set, exact Φ on both) is unrun; until it runs the crossing is a reading and the draft correctly says so — the author decides whether to build it. (6) The author-owned temper paragraph (guard watch-item above) needs the author's sign-off.

verdict.post:
ADVERSARIAL FACT-CHECK — Post 4, "Where Hegel Files the Microscope"

I tried to break the digest on receipts, metadata, camps, quotes, loci, and framing. Most of it holds under direct verification against the repo and against the actual source texts (a full local cache of the di Giovanni Science of Logic, the Brinkmann & Dahlstrom Encyclopedia epub, the Kreines/Ebeturk/Koch article texts, and the Guyer & Matthews Kant sits in the session scratchpad, so I checked wording line by line rather than trusting the specialist's read). Two defects survived; neither sinks the thesis, but both must be fixed before the quotes enter the library or the rewrite.

LAB RECEIPTS — all confirmed against the code. probe_resilience.py is Probe 108 (D2) with N=3, MAX=30, recovery-time-vs-verdict correlation. probe_attractor_condition.py is Probe 130 (P1), restricted to n_bidir==3, testing max_period / n_fixed / n_reachable against the binary verdict. STRUCTURAL_FINDINGS #7 says exactly what the digest says: proxies recover the verdict only near chance (rank-AUC ≤ 0.63), exact Φ needed and feasible because coordination units are small; the contrast figure (bidirectional-coupling + influence ≥ 0.75 at rank-AUC 0.89 over 256 determinations) sits at lines 79–80. The absence receipt is real: a grep with --include=*.py returns zero chemism / acid / self-production model files. The receipts are safe to cite as written.

METADATA — all confirmed. Ebeturk, Hegel Bulletin 44(1):46–73 (2023); Koch, 44(1):148–170 (2023); both in the "Hegel and Teleology" special issue (guest editors Maraguat and Kreines — a bonus the digest could note). Kreines, ch. 13 of the Cambridge Companion to Hegel and Nineteenth-Century Philosophy, ed. Beiser (2008). Ng, Hegel's Concept of Life (OUP 2020), ch. 2 "Kant's Great Service to Philosophy." No camp error: the digest assigns functional roles (anchor / threat / prior-art), not metaphysical-vs-non-metaphysical labels, and its use of Kreines and Ng to power the replacement-not-anticipation reading is faithful to both.

QUOTES — the load-bearing set is verbatim. The crossing exhibit (di Giovanni SL 645–649: "belong to its nature," "not comprehensible from itself, and the being of one object is the being of another," "tranquil neutrality," "does not spontaneously re-start... it did not posit it," "these three syllogisms fall apart," "re-activated only by a differentiation"), plus p. 654 ("greatest services," "the higher principle, the concept in its concrete existence," "a principle of freedom") and p. 663 ("the plough is more honorable than are immediately..."), all match. Kreines p. 344/346 verbatim. Ebeturk p. 57 ("the chemical process as a whole is the self-determination of the concept in and through distinctive objective processes") verbatim. Koch p. 162 ("there are no objects without such teleological structures. The constitution of objects is ontologically dependent on teleological structures") verbatim. The Kant CPJ quotes check out. And I closed one of the digest's own gates: BOTH B&D pins are verbatim in the actual Brinkmann & Dahlstrom text — "Addition 2. Objectivity contains the three forms: mechanism, chemism, and the relation of purpose" and "Through the concept of inner purposiveness, Kant re-awakened the idea in general and that of life in particular." The digest marked these merely "gated"; the wording is now verified, and only the print page numbers (270, 277) remain to spot-check.

TWO DEFECTS. (1) Koch p. 149 is misquoted — in the digest's secondary key_claim AND in the draft itself (post4_ladder.md line 295), the phrase "structures of external purposiveness constitute mechanical objects" appears inside quotation marks with a page pin. Koch never wrote that. His text reads "structures of external purposiveness provide the conditions for the individuation of mechanical objects." The substitution matters: Koch is deliberately careful that external purposiveness conditions individuation, not that it constitutes objects, and "constitute mechanical objects" appears in his article only negated and about mechanical structures ("mechanical structures alone do not... constitute mechanical objects"). (2) The digest's primary_passages table mislabels the §213 boundary as "SL pp. 268, 282 / di Giovanni (Cambridge 2010)" and marks it "verified." The draft correctly cites those pages to the Encyclopedia (Brinkmann & Dahlstrom, 1830/2010a), and §194–§213 are Encyclopedia section numbers, not Science of Logic; di Giovanni SL pp. 268/282 fall in the Doctrine of Essence, nowhere near Objectivity. Anyone citing the digest literally would attach the wrong edition to the boundary pin.

GUARD — clean. The draft refuses anticipation explicitly ("He does not anticipate a causal-irreducibility criterion... He replaces it") and never demotes Φ ("The instrument's contribution is not diminished by having a ceiling"). Homology (same-boundary/different-instrument) is preserved; no identity claim smuggled in. The temper-paragraph watch-item is an author-voice call, not a citation issue, and the digest flags it correctly.

Verdict: needs-correction. Fix the Koch quote and the digest's edition label, treat the two B&D quotes as verified-wording, and the post's one original result — the crossing inside chemism — stands on verbatim text.

corrections.target: Koch p. 149 quote (digest secondary_sources koch2023 key_claim; and draft post4_ladder.md line 295)
corrections.problem: The words "structures of external purposiveness constitute mechanical objects" are set in quotation marks with a page pin as if verbatim, but Koch did not write them. Her actual sentence is "structures of external purposiveness provide the conditions for the individuation of mechanical objects." "Constitute mechanical objects" appears in the article only in a negated clause about mechanical structures. The paraphrase-as-quote also overstates Koch, who is careful that external purposiveness conditions individuation rather than constituting objects.
corrections.fix: Replace with the verbatim wording "structures of external purposiveness provide the conditions for the individuation of mechanical objects" (Koch 2023), or drop the quotation marks and present it as paraphrase. The argument loses nothing: the verbatim p. 162 quote ("there are no objects without such teleological structures. The constitution of objects is ontologically dependent on teleological structures") already carries the object-dependence claim and is accurate.

corrections.target: Digest primary_passages entry #2: "SL pp. 268, 282 (§213 boundary)," edition "di Giovanni (Cambridge 2010)," verified "verified"
corrections.problem: Wrong edition and wrong verification status. The draft (post4_ladder.md lines 49-50) cites pp. 268/282 to the Encyclopedia (Brinkmann & Dahlstrom, 1830/2010a), and §194-§213 are Encyclopedia section numbers, not Science of Logic. In di Giovanni's SL, pp. 268/282 fall in the Doctrine of Essence, far from Objectivity, so the label "di Giovanni SL" is a category error that would mis-cite the boundary if copied into the rewrite. Marking it "verified" also contradicts the digest's own "gated" status for the identical one-source B&D pagination.
corrections.fix: Relabel the entry to Brinkmann & Dahlstrom, Encyclopedia Logic (2010a), pp. 268, 282, and change status from "verified" to "gated" alongside the other B&D page pins (wording of the boundary is structurally correct; only the print page numbers remain to spot-check).
